Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-03 15:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Tom Brooks (Redwood AE), Anita Chandra (Redwood SE), Javier Morales (Redwood CSM), Mark Li (NovaMart VP Eng), Rhea Patel (NovaMart Head ML Platform), Samir Khan (NovaMart Security), Emily Zhou (NovaMart Product)

Summary (auto): 58-minute QBR-style check-in. Focus on upcoming seasonal scale, cost-econ levers, and private VPC pilot checklist. Several action items assigned.

[00:00] Tom (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, Tom Brooks here from Redwood, i'm joined by Anita and javier. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Mark (NovaMart VP Eng): good, morning — afternoon — yeah thanks for setting this up. we had a couple of traffic spikes last week so excited to talk through the mitigation plan.
[00:25] Rhea (NovaMart): hi all, Rhea here. main goals: make sure inference scales for holiday prep, reduce per-unit cost, and validate private deployment constraints.
[00:38] Anita (Redwood SE): great, we prepared a short playbook and some numbers. i'll run through usage trends then cost levers: batching, prefix caching, and quantization profiles.
[00:48] [background: faint typing]
[01:02] Anita: so NovaMart's 99th percentile latency budget is 250ms for cart-suggestions, is that still correct?
[01:08] Mark: yes that's the target. we can tolerate a small percent of slower responses during spikes but need graceful degradation.
[01:15] Tom: perfect. quick snapshot — your hosted usage grew 3.2x over the last 30 days, peak burst hours are more concentrated, which makes batching more effective but also risks queueing.
[01:30] Samir (Security): quick interject, on hosted vs private — our compliance team wants KMS integration and VPC isolation for PII-ish logs. is that supported in Redwood Private?
[01:40] Javier (Redwood CSM): yep, private supports customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, and the private control plane with audit logs. we can share our SOC 2 docs and the VPC checklist.
[01:52] Samir: awesome, we'll send a list of required policies after this call.
[02:01] Rhea: on cost, we ran a quick estimate and saw a 28% spend increase month-over-month; we'd like concrete levers to push it down by at least 15% before peak.
[02:12] Anita: the quick wins are: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated session traffic, tune batching windows for peak vs tail, and try int8 quantization on the smaller models. we can model impact live.
[02:28] Emily (Product): can you explain the tradeoff between batching and tail latency? our UX team is concerned about tail spikes.
[02:36] Anita: yes — batching reduces per-token GPU cost because multiple requests share compute. but if you wait too long to accumulate a batch, user-visible latency increases for requests arriving during a quiet period. Redwood's runtime uses adaptive batching: it short-circuits when SLOs approach thresholds, but in extremes you still see tail increases.
[02:58] Mark: do we have numbers for 99/95 latencies with the adaptive batching on our workload?
[03:06] Anita: initial synthetic numbers suggest 95th ~120ms, 99th ~260ms with default batching. with prefix caching for personalized prompts, 95th drops to ~90ms and 99th to ~210ms. caveat: transcription errors in earlier tests, but we have tests to validate.
[03:26] [crosstalk] Tom: i'm going to share the cost model shortly — it shows per-route economics if you push caching and a dedicated pool for high-throughput routes.
[03:39] Tom: question for NovaMart — what percentage of traffic would you put into a dedicated pool if we offered burst capacity?
[03:47] Mark: top 3 routes account for ~65% of tokens. we'd likely reserve dedicated capacity for those and leave long-tail on hosted.
[03:56] Rhea: yes that sounds right. but we need a playbook for fallback if the dedicated pool degrades.
[04:03] Anita: we recommend automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in hosted mode with a traffic-shaping policy and throttles. the control plane supports canary rollbacks and route-level fallbacks.
[04:16] Emily: any impact to personalization quality with fallback?
[04:20] Anita: small. if you fallback to a quantized model or a smaller family, you may see a small regress in metrics; we'll tie that to eval prompts.
[04:30] Samir: about logs — we need to confirm retention and PII redaction. are request/response bodies ever stored in plaintext?
[04:38] Javier: by default logs are redacted for sensitive fields; with Private you control retention and storage. we'll share the audit log spec and our compliance pack.
[04:48] Samir: okay send that.
[04:52] Tom: moving on — cost scenarios. i'm going to screen-share the model (note: in transcript the share link was posted).
[05:00] [link shared: cost-model-v3.xlsx]
[05:06] Tom: overview: three scenarios — baseline (hosted, no caching), hybrid (caching + batching tweaks), and dedicated (reserved pool for top routes). baseline cost per 1M tokens is X; hybrid reduces ~22-30% depending on cache hit; dedicated reduces further but with commit costs.
[05:25] Mark: what are the ongoing ops tradeoffs with dedicated? more SLAs but more runbook responsibility?
[05:32] Anita: Redwood Dedicated comes with SLA-backed throughput and optional managed autoscaling policies. ops-wise you'll need to own model version pinning and rollout policy decisions, but we provide the console dashboards and tracing hooks.
[05:48] Rhea: curious about quantization risk — you mentioned int8 earlier, how risky is that for our NLU tasks?
[05:55] Anita: for generation it's usually safe with post-quant evals, but for exact-match or legal verbiage might be sensitive. recommend progressive rollout with evals tied to key prompts.
[06:08] [00:06:08 on timer beep — irrelevant]
[06:12] Mark: can Anita run a targeted quantization eval on our prompt set?
[06:15] Anita: yes that's an action; i'll schedule the 24h benchmark and run both int8 and 4bit quantized variants against your top routes.
[06:24] Tom: we'll need telemetry: token-level cost, latency by route, and per-tenant tracing. javier, can you confirm we can expose those in the console?
[06:33] Javier: yes — token breakdown, model-level latencies, and sample traces are available. exportable CSVs and tracing endpoints exist.
[06:41] Emily: timeline question — if we do a private VPC pilot, how long from sign-off to first traffic?
[06:48] Tom: typical on-prem/VPC lead time is 4-8 weeks depending on customer infra readiness. if you're on cloud with VPC peering it's closer to 2-3 weeks.
[06:58] Rhea: our infra team prefers VPC peering rather than on-prem initially. can we get a checklist?
[07:05] Anita: yes — we'll send the VPC checklist and a sample terraform snippet.
[07:12] Samir: for KMS, do you support customer-managed keys in all deployment modes?
[07:18] Javier: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated; hosted has envelope encryption but not full customer KMS. we'll map that out in the security doc.
[07:31] Mark: perf question — during last spike we saw sudden KV cache misses, what's best practice for cache warm-up during pre-season traffic?
[07:40] Anita: warm-up runs are recommended: pre-load common prefixes and keep-alive sessions. also pre-warming the dedicated pool with synthetic traffic helps reduce cold starts.
[07:50] Tom: we also recommend scheduled canary traffic increases to validate autoscaling thresholds.
[07:56] Rhea: about cost commitment — if we reserve capacity, what's the minimum term?
[08:02] Tom: typical commitments are monthly or annual, with discounts for annual. we can model partial month ramping for seasonality.
[08:12] Emily: how do we measure quality regressions if we change models or quantize?
[08:17] Anita: Redwood supports eval suites tied to prompt sets and you can configure regression thresholds. we'll hook into your metrics so regressions trigger alerts and automatic rollback if desired.
[08:30] [pause / background noise]
[08:42] Mark: can you give a concrete cost-savings estimate if we adopt hybrid caching + dedicated for top routes?
[08:50] Tom: based on your numbers, hybrid could save ~25% and a conservative dedicated commit focused on top routes could save 35-40% net after amortizing reserved cost across peak windows. specifics in the spreadsheet.
[09:05] Rhea: are there hidden costs for higher throughput like network egress?
[09:10] Anita: network costs are separate; if you run Private in your VPC network egress stays within your cloud billing; hosted has some bandwidth cost implications depending on region. we'll include that line item.
[09:22] Samir: on audit logs — do we get immutable logs for compliance?
[09:27] Javier: yes, audit logs are stored with options for immutability and longer retention in Private. we'll send the retention matrix.
[09:35] Emily: next steps — what do we need to sign-off on to start a pilot?
[09:40] Tom: decision points: commit to a scope (routes + traffic percentage), choose deployment mode (VPC pilot recommended), and sign an MSA addendum for Dedicated/Private if needed.
[09:51] [link posted: security-pack-v2.pdf]
[09:58] Samir: i'll review the security pack and send questions.
[10:02] Anita: action recap — i'll run the quantization eval and 24h stress test; Tom will update the cost model; javier and samir will follow on SOC2/KMS.
[10:12] Tom: all right let's call out dates: Tom to share cost model by 2026-08-06, Anita to run bench and share by 2026-08-10, Samir to send policy list 2026-08-07.
[10:24] Mark: that works, thanks everyone. any blockers?
[10:28] Rhea: none besides waiting for the security checklist.
[10:32] Tom: i'll also send a proposed pilot schedule for the week of Aug 17.
[10:36] Emily: thanks, appreciate the clear next steps.
[10:40] [00:10:40 small side conversation about calendar invites omitted]
[10:50] Tom: final note — we'll instrument a rollback playbook in the console and share a runbook draft.
[10:57] Mark: good to have — thanks.
[11:02] Tom: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread.
